evidence: A green HTTP candidate serving the marker passed its cycle; progress showed the eleven specified effects in order, all recorded, with gate-attempt-passed at the gate.
After R-1 failed at fence, starting R-1 for C-2 returned run-already-started; the progress list contained exactly R-1 for C-1.
While R-1’s builder slept, a concurrent R-2 start was refused run-in-progress and R-1 progress was still running; Grain held only one run-started event.
After R-1 passed, a start for R-2 on the same cycle returned cycle-already-run; Grain contained only one run-started event.
Sent start-run for the absent deadbeef commit against a fixture git repository; it returned not-a-commit, and run-progress returned null with no builder configured or launched.
A committed slice with no scenarios produced a checklist effect refused empty-checklist; progress showed a pre-cycle checklist halt and no self-check or fence effects.
With two stamped scenarios and an additional untagged scenario, start-run recorded the two imports then halted at stamp for an unstamped scenario; progress showed no pin or checklist effect.

A fresh cut imported 06-001, 06-003 and 06-076 in order and showed next-number 77, and an untagged cut halted at stamp. A later cut with duplicate 06-001 identities nevertheless ran through self-check, fence and scoring instead of halting; the direct command to seed a retired identity also returned -32601.
A self-check exiting 1 with last line golden checklist differs produced harness-self-check-failed; progress showed the cycle failed at fence with that detail, and no fence or regenerate effect.
A self-check printing SKIP bb-tools and exiting zero produced harness-self-check-passed, with skipped-checks containing bb-tools and the detail naming the skip.
The cut contained impl but not harness/cycles; the fence effect was refused fenced-path-matched-nothing and the next effect failed the cycle at fence for fence-refused, before any builder launch.

The builder observed the plan and config, an empty scope, one commit and no fenced paths in the reachable object listing. Its git ls-tree showed provided-runtime as mode 160000 with the same object ID as the cut.
The builder logged one session and supplied a red first candidate, with a green second candidate prepared; the run failed after attempt 1 and never launched the required repair session.
The builder copied a candidate and exited 1; regenerate recorded its candidate digest and the run passed with its cycle.
An executable builder that exited zero without writing a candidate led to a recorded fail-cycle effect and a regenerate-stage candidate-not-regenerated failure; no regenerate effect was recorded.
A builder recorded its PID and slept with a two-second regenerate budget; the PID had exited and progress showed the cycle failed at regenerate for budget.

A server occupied the configured port before gating and the candidate launch marker stayed absent, but the run halted effect-could-not-run at gate instead of recording three seam-answered-before-boot refusals and failing for infrastructure.
A one-attempt fixture with a red test.sh recorded gate-attempt-failed for suite-red and then gate-attempts-exhausted; its launch marker was absent.
A candidate containing test.sh but no start.sh produced gate-attempt-failed for contract-missing on attempt 1.
A green candidate served a page without the configured sauna marker; the one gate attempt recorded gate-attempt-failed for identity-probe-failed.
A builder left a green candidate and a delayed child turned its builder-room suite red after exit; that suite later exited 1, while the gate copy passed. The regenerate and install digests matched.

The red first candidate failed its gate, but the builder log contained only the first launch and progress had no repair effect. The required second room and read-only evidence mounts were never produced.

With a red candidate and a budget allowing three gate attempts, progress failed the cycle for gate-attempts-exhausted after attempt 1, with no repair or attempts 2 and 3. The required three failed attempts did not occur.
The grader returned one valid pass and no row for 01-002; file-verdicts offered only 01-001, and Measurement filed 01-002 unreached with 1 of 2 passing while the cycle passed.
R-1 failed at fence and R-2 halted at an empty checklist; repeated progress reads five seconds later were identical to the first reads, retaining failed and halted respectively.
After the cycle passed, two run-progress queries returned identical run objects, both showing passed.
The cut probe accepted only the single configured HTTP URL and verified the marker there; gate-attempt-passed was recorded and the cycle passed.
The candidate suite created and removed a directory inside its scope, after which the gate passed; regenerate and install events had the same digest.
The passing self-check printed the full legacy SKIP line; the recorded self-check passed and its detail and skipped-checks included the complete text after SKIP.
The green stdio suite, probe and store check produced gate-attempt-passed with 30 seconds, one poll, answered on poll 1 and probe text answered as the context; the cycle passed without gate refusals.

The stdio probe recorded gate-1/impl/start.sh and 30 as its two arguments, with GATE_STORE under gate-evidence-1 outside the gate room and no LOYLY_ variables. The store check recorded that same events.sqlite path.
The red stdio suite recorded its environment, which contained neither LOYLY_ variables nor GATE_STORE; the gate failed for suite-red and neither probe nor store-check marker appeared.
A failing stdio identity probe printed the 30-second no-response line; the gate recorded identity-probe-failed with that detail, and the store-check marker was absent.
A passing stdio probe followed by a failing store check produced identity-probe-failed with the exact FAIL event 7 line, and the cycle failed at gate for gate-attempts-exhausted.
A stdio candidate whose suite required plan/01-spec/spec.feature passed its gate; the regenerate and install events carried the same candidate digest.
A green stdio candidate and passing identity probe with no store-check command halted at gate with effect-could-not-run; progress recorded no gate effect.
Two stdio runs on the same store used store-check commands ending in one and two; both first self-checks passed, and their harness digests differed.
A committed plan/01-a symlink to ../spec/a produced a recorded stamp and a checklist containing 01-001 and 01-002 with source plan/01-a/spec.feature; the run concluded rather than halting.
With slices 01 and 02 present and PLAN_SLICES=02, the only stamp imported 02-001 and the checklist contained 02-001 alone.

The first builder received the configured image as its third argument, but regenerate detail was empty and omitted its name and digest. No repair launch or repair effect occurred after its red candidate.
The config named builder-clojure in an empty image directory; start-run refused builder-image-missing and run-progress returned null before any builder launch.
Two runs on one store passed; the second stamp emitted no new identities, and measurement/scoreboard for C-2 named C-1 as previous-cycle-id.
A cut probe read harness/config.sh relative to itself and verified the served marker; attempt 1 passed and install and regenerate carried the same digest.

The gate command received the cut tree without impl, the candidate copy matching the install digest, and an empty evidence directory, from the project repository; the candidate launch marker was absent. Its BOOT 20 10, ANSWERED 3 and final probe line produced the corresponding gate-attempt-passed event.

The first command wrote its evidence and reported suite-red 3 of 65 tests failed, which was recorded correctly. The runner then ended after attempt 1 without a repair builder or a second gate attempt, despite a three-attempt budget.

The command printed BOOT 20 10 followed by seam-answered-before-boot and exited 1; the runner halted at gate as effect-could-not-run after one launch, instead of recording three refusals and failing the cycle for infrastructure.

The command printed BOOT 20 10 then the unrecognized infrastructure line and exited 2; progress halted at gate with no gate, fail-cycle, or cycle. Its halt detail included the preceding BOOT line instead of the specified last line alone.

Three passing runs without a gate command and with gate-a and gate-b had three different harness digests. The no-command digest 06561766... did not equal SHA-256 of the configuration bytes, self-check command text and probe bytes concatenated in that order (46bd0e85...).
The green HTTP run passed with the eleven specified effects. Grain’s event-store checker accepted every model event as lying within its named leaf of a completed cycle.v2 run or delegated child tick.

A server returned 503 for its first three requests and then served the marker; the gate passed with 20 polls, 10 seconds and answered-on-poll 5. The required attempt margin could not be observed: regeneration-cycle/cycle-progress returned -32601 and run-progress did not expose it.
A red first candidate with a green repair prepared failed after attempt 1 with no repair or second gate. The Grain trace showed cycle.v2 alone and no gate-attempt.v1 child tick.
A candidate copy in a temporary directory outside any .pi ancestor ran a green HTTP fixture; progress showed gate-attempt-passed and the cycle passed. The temporary copy was removed after profiling.

The host returned booked/pass and no receipt/fail; the filed measurement contained 1 of 2 passing and the cycle passed. Grain held checklist/01-001 score 1.0 and checklist/01-002 score 0.0 in two distinct grade.v2 child ticks of the cycle tick.
The first host returned E-ONE and its score carried that feedback; inspection of the second grading room and instruction found no E-ONE.

The permitted grading room contained no real Pi grader host or policy manifest, so I could not launch the required Pi session or observe its Linux shell and host mounts. With the host unset, the runner stopped progressing after checklist and produced no grading room or VM trace; the isolation Then was not observed.

The host returned a booked pass and an empty-evidence pass; only 01-001 was scored or offered in file-verdicts, and Grain held only its judge score. Measurement filed 1 of 2 passing with 01-002 unreached.
The approved list contained r-1 while the computed sealed grader digest differed; progress halted at grader with the actual digest, before any self-check, fence, or builder launch.
A host writing no verdict rows led file-verdicts to refuse zero-verdicts, followed by fail-score-stage; the cycle failed for score-stage-failed and the builder log contained only its original launch.

After stopping the runner and its sleeping builder five seconds into the first launch, I restarted on the same store and polled progress for 40 seconds. R-1 remained running at five effects and the session log contained only one launch, so it neither resumed the builder nor passed.

The model returned ORC markers around INSTRUCTION-7, but the builder instruction retained those markers instead of exactly INSTRUCTION-7. After its red suite the run ended at attempt 1, so no repair instruction was produced.
The model stub returned HTTP 500 to the render request; progress halted at render for effect-could-not-run, with no regenerate, fail-cycle, cycle, or builder marker.

While the builder slept, run-progress showed R-1 running and five completed effect results through fence, but returned no tick identity or node list; the required render and running regenerate nodes were absent.

Measurement filed one pass out of two with 01-002 unreached; the two tagged Allure results matched those statuses and reasons. A separate fresh-store run produced the same history and case IDs for both items.

The 01-001 host started a child and exceeded its three-second deadline; both recorded PIDs were gone, and Grain held one judge score while progress named 01-002 alone. Measurement filed 01-001 unreached, with no additional regenerate effect.

The builder fixture recorded model-A; the 01-001 grader launch also reported model-A and 01-002 reported model-B. Progress scored both as passes and Measurement filed both, so the builder-model row was not rejected as required.
